claims.title: Graph-basis stabilizer-query weighted-Hamming geometry
claims.scope: finite graph-state basis labels under a declared probability distribution over stabilizer-generator queries
assumptions: the state family is |G,z>=Z^z|G> for one fixed simple graph
query i measures K_i=X_i product_{j in N(i)} Z_j
the generator-query distribution is identical under the compared labels
nonclaims: does not establish a metric for arbitrary quantum states or observables
does not convert internal predictive distance into parent-substrate cost

claims.title: Cycle graph two-local blindness with three-local label queries
claims.scope: graph-basis states of the simple cycle C_n for n at least five
assumptions: local reductions are evaluated through the exact graph-state stabilizer support criterion
label recovery queries are the weight-three graph stabilizer generators
nonclaims: identical one- and two-body marginals do not imply indistinguishability after arbitrary global transcript aggregation
does not describe generic many-body matter

claims.title: Finite Gilbert predictive packing for graph-basis labels
claims.scope: uniform stabilizer-generator queries on n graph-basis label bits with total-variation tolerance epsilon
assumptions: predictive approximation is measured in one-query total variation
one renderer state induces one approximating future query law
nonclaims: the asymptotic entropy rate is not substituted for the finite Hamming-ball certificate
does not claim every physical quantum family realizes this code

claims.title: Cat-state proper-marginal phase blindness
claims.scope: local X measurements of a declared ell-qubit phase-labeled cat state
assumptions: each recorded local outcome is an X-basis eigenvalue
nonclaims: proper-marginal blindness does not prevent a complete distributed transcript from revealing the phase
does not imply that arbitrary entangled states have the same parity law

claims.title: Exact online cat-parity consistency memory
claims.scope: m independent cat blocks after ell-1 local X outcomes have been emitted in each block
assumptions: future queries request the final X outcome of a selected block
the renderer must reproduce the exact parity-constrained transcript law
predictive equivalence is defined by all allowed future block queries
nonclaims: the renderer need not retain the full emitted transcript because one parity bit per block is sufficient
the m internal bits are not asserted to be m parent-hardware bits

claims.title: Constant-tolerance relational memory rate
claims.scope: the declared uniform generator-query or final-block-query normalized-Hamming models
assumptions: epsilon lies below one quarter for the positive asymptotic Gilbert rate
binary label codes are admissible hidden predictive states
nonclaims: the asymptotic rate is model-dependent and is not an empirical estimate about the universe
finite block-length claims use the explicit Gilbert size bound
